4. Atomic data for astrophysics. I. Radiative recombination rates for H-like, He-like, Li-like and Na-like ions over a broad range of temperature ID: c6m4at4dwfhi 2022 · Ferland, G. J. DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.astro-ph/9509083 Abstract: We present new calculations and analytic fits to the rates of radiative recombination towards H-like, He-like, Li-like and Na-like ions of all elements from H through Zn (Z=30). The fits are valid over a wide range of temperature, from 3 K to 10**9 K. 5. Partial Photoionization Cross Sections and Radiative Recombination Rate Coefficients for Lithium-Like Ions ID: 3mkf36ulir 1979 · W. D. Barfield · The Astrophysical Journal DOI: 10.1086/157021 Abstract: Partial photoionization cross sections and radiative recombination rate coefficients corresponding to n=2, 3, 4, and 6, and l0.03 keV), O) kT>0.1), and Al(kT>1.0). 6. Photoionization of Li and radiative recombination of Li + in Debye plasmas ID: 4exswnodr3 2009 · Yue Ying Qi, Ying Wu, Jianguo Wang · Physics of Plasmas DOI: 10.1063/1.3098544 Abstract: The photoionization cross sections in the photoelectron energy below 2 Ry are calculated for the ground and n≤4 excited states of Li embedded in plasma environments and the radiative-recombination (RR) rate coefficients for Li+ were presented for temperature T=100–32 000 K in a wide range of plasma parameters. The plasma screening interaction is described by the Debye–Huckel model and the energy levels and wave functions including both the bound and continuum states are calculated by solving the Schrodinger equation numerically in a symplectic integration scheme. The screening of Coulomb interactions remarkably changes the photoionization cross sections near the ionization threshold, and especially for the ns states, the Cooper minimum is uncovered and shifted to the higher energy as the screening interaction increases. The RR rate coefficients at low temperature have a complex variation on the Debye lengths; whereas at higher temperature the RR rate coefficients decrease with the increasing of screening ... 7. Chianti—an atomic database for emission lines. xii. version 7 of the database ID: 4y5jdtauvc 2012 · Enrico Landi, G. Del Zanna, Peter R. Young · The Astrophysical Journal DOI: 10.1088/0004-637X/744/2/99 Abstract: The CHIANTI spectral code consists of an atomic database and a suite of computer programs to calculate the optically thin spectrum of astrophysical objects and carry out spectroscopic plasma diagnostics. The database includes atomic energy levels, wavelengths, radiative transition probabilities, collision excitation rate coefficients, and ionization and recombination rate coefficients, as well as data to calculate free-free, free-bound, and two-photon continuum emission. Version 7 has been released, which includes several new ions, significant updates to existing ions, as well as Chianti-Py, the implementation of CHIANTI software in the Python programming language. All data and programs are freely available at http://www.chiantidatabase.org, while the Python interface to CHIANTI can be found at http://chiantipy.sourceforge.net. 8. A Public Code for Precision Big Bang Nucleosynthesis with Improved Helium-4 Predictions ID: 1fk0pisyrl 2019 · A. Coc, Cyril Pitrou, Jean-Philippe Uzan DOI: 10.1007/978-3-030-13876-9_57 Abstract: A Mathematica code (“PRIMAT”) for big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN), has been made publicly available. Its network includes more than 400 reactions with their updated thermonuclear reaction rates. In particular, it takes advantage of the recently improved weak reaction rates that include all the required theoretical corrections to reach a level of accuracy of \(10^{-4}\) on \(^4\mathrm{He}\). Once the uncertainties on the reaction rates and neutron lifetime are taken into account, we obtain \(Y_p = 0.24709 \pm 0.00017\), D/H = (\(2.459 \pm 0.036) \times 10^{-5}\) and Li/H = (\(5.623 \pm 0.247)\times 10^{-10}\). 9. A theoretical treatment of the LiH and BeH formation through radiative association ID: 5dskhbexpc 1999 · Marie-Christine Bacchus-Montabonel, D. Talbi · Journal of Molecular Structure-theochem DOI: 10.1016/S0166-1280(98)00397-2 Abstract: Rate constants for the formation of LiH and BeH through the radiative association process have been calculated from potential energy surfaces and dipole moments, accurately determined using quantum chemistry methods. At 400 K, these rate constants are 0.3×10−19 cm3 s−1 for LiH and 0.7×10−19 cm3 s−1 for BeH. The cosmological implications of these results and the role of LiH and BeH as primordial molecules are discussed. 10. Time of primordial Be-7 conversion into Li-7, energy release and doublet of narrow cosmological neutrino lines ID: 2pjzrrnact4s 2022 · Khatri, Rishi, Sunyaev, Rashid A. DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.1009.3932 Abstract: One of the important light elements created during the big bang nucleosynthesis is Be-7 which then decays to Li-7 by electron capture when recombination becomes effective but well before the Saha equilibrium recombination is reached. This means that Be-7 should wait until its recombination epoch even though the half-life of the hydrogenic beryllium atom is only 106.4 days. We calculate when the conversion from primordial Be-7 to Li-7 occurs taking into account the population of the hyperfine structure sublevels and solving the kinetic equations for recombination, photoionization and conversion rate. We also calculate the energies and the spectrum of narrow neutrino doublet lines resulting from Be-7 decay.

papers.title: Atomic data for astrophysics. I. Radiative recombination rates for H-like, He-like, Li-like and Na-like ions over a broad range of temperature
papers.abstract: We present new calculations and analytic fits to the rates of radiative recombination towards H-like, He-like, Li-like and Na-like ions of all elements from H through Zn (Z=30). The fits are valid over a wide range of temperature, from 3 K to 10**9 K.

papers.title: Photoionization of Li and radiative recombination of Li + in Debye plasmas
papers.abstract: The photoionization cross sections in the photoelectron energy below 2 Ry are calculated for the ground and n≤4 excited states of Li embedded in plasma environments and the radiative-recombination (RR) rate coefficients for Li+ were presented for temperature T=100–32 000 K in a wide range of plasma parameters. The plasma screening interaction is described by the Debye–Huckel model and the energy levels and wave functions including both the bound and continuum states are calculated by solving the Schrodinger equation numerically in a symplectic integration scheme. The screening of Coulomb interactions remarkably changes the photoionization cross sections near the ionization threshold, and especially for the ns states, the Cooper minimum is uncovered and shifted to the higher energy as the screening interaction increases. The RR rate coefficients at low temperature have a complex variation on the Debye lengths; whereas at higher temperature the RR rate coefficients decrease with the increasing of screening ...
papers.tldr: The photoionization cross sections in the photoelectron energy below 2 Ry are calculated for the ground and n≤4 excited states of Li embedded in plasma environments and the radiative-recombination (RR) rate coefficients for Li+ were presented for temperature T=100−32'000'K in a wide range of plasma parameters as mentioned in this paper.

papers.title: Chianti—an atomic database for emission lines. xii. version 7 of the database
papers.abstract: The CHIANTI spectral code consists of an atomic database and a suite of computer programs to calculate the optically thin spectrum of astrophysical objects and carry out spectroscopic plasma diagnostics. The database includes atomic energy levels, wavelengths, radiative transition probabilities, collision excitation rate coefficients, and ionization and recombination rate coefficients, as well as data to calculate free-free, free-bound, and two-photon continuum emission. Version 7 has been released, which includes several new ions, significant updates to existing ions, as well as Chianti-Py, the implementation of CHIANTI software in the Python programming language. All data and programs are freely available at http://www.chiantidatabase.org, while the Python interface to CHIANTI can be found at http://chiantipy.sourceforge.net.
papers.tldr: The CHIANTI spectral code consists of an atomic database and a suite of computer programs to calculate the optically thin spectrum of astrophysical objects and carry out spectroscopic plasma diagnostics as discussed by the authors.

papers.title: A Public Code for Precision Big Bang Nucleosynthesis with Improved Helium-4 Predictions
papers.abstract: A Mathematica code (“PRIMAT”) for big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN), has been made publicly available. Its network includes more than 400 reactions with their updated thermonuclear reaction rates. In particular, it takes advantage of the recently improved weak reaction rates that include all the required theoretical corrections to reach a level of accuracy of \(10^{-4}\) on \(^4\mathrm{He}\). Once the uncertainties on the reaction rates and neutron lifetime are taken into account, we obtain \(Y_p = 0.24709 \pm 0.00017\), D/H = (\(2.459 \pm 0.036) \times 10^{-5}\) and Li/H = (\(5.623 \pm 0.247)\times 10^{-10}\).
papers.tldr: A Mathematica code for big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) has been made publicly available as discussed by the authors, which includes more than 400 BBN reactions with their updated thermonuclear reaction rates.

papers.title: A theoretical treatment of the LiH and BeH formation through radiative association
papers.abstract: Rate constants for the formation of LiH and BeH through the radiative association process have been calculated from potential energy surfaces and dipole moments, accurately determined using quantum chemistry methods. At 400 K, these rate constants are 0.3×10−19 cm3 s−1 for LiH and 0.7×10−19 cm3 s−1 for BeH. The cosmological implications of these results and the role of LiH and BeH as primordial molecules are discussed.
papers.tldr: In this paper, the cosmological implications of these results and the role of LiH and BeH as primordial molecules are discussed, as well as their role in the formation of the universe.

papers.title: Time of primordial Be-7 conversion into Li-7, energy release and doublet of narrow cosmological neutrino lines
papers.abstract: One of the important light elements created during the big bang nucleosynthesis is Be-7 which then decays to Li-7 by electron capture when recombination becomes effective but well before the Saha equilibrium recombination is reached. This means that Be-7 should wait until its recombination epoch even though the half-life of the hydrogenic beryllium atom is only 106.4 days. We calculate when the conversion from primordial Be-7 to Li-7 occurs taking into account the population of the hyperfine structure sublevels and solving the kinetic equations for recombination, photoionization and conversion rate. We also calculate the energies and the spectrum of narrow neutrino doublet lines resulting from Be-7 decay.
